AT THE SFC...LOW NOW OVER NW OK WILL MOVE STEADILY NE THROUGH THE PERIOD...REACHING CNTRL MO THIS EVE AND SW MI BY 12Z WED. sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: PRIMARY UPPER LEVEL IMPULSE OF CONCERN TODAY/TONIGHT IS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH CURRENTLY MOVING EWD INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS. THIS LEAD IMPULSE WILL BECOME NEGATIVELY TILTED AS IT MOVES E/NEWD INTO MO THIS EVENING AND THE OH VALLEY TONIGHT. AN UPSTREAM SPEED MAX ACROSS THE PAC NW WILL AMPLIFY SOMEWHAT AS IT MOVES INTO THE CENTRAL ROCKIES BY 12Z WED. A SURFACE LOW CURRENTLY OVER S-CENTRAL KS WILL MOVE EWD INTO SWRN MO THIS EVENING AND THEN NEWD INTO LOWER MI BY 12Z WED IN TANDEM WITH THE UPPER IMPULSE. A DRYLINE WILL EXTEND SWWD FROM THE SURFACE LOW INTO ERN OK/WRN PORTIONS OF NORTH TX BY LATE AFTN AND A WARM FRONT SHOULD EXTEND FROM E OF THE SFC LOW ACROSS SRN MO/FAR SRN IL.

sections.title: ERN PORTIONS OF SRN/CENTRAL PLAINS EWD TO LOWER OH VALLEY
sections.text: IN THE WAKE OF OVERNIGHT CONVECTION ACROSS PORTIONS OF ERN KS/NERN OK AND MUCH OF MO...A COOL/MOIST AIR MASS IS IN PLACE WITH TEMPS AVERAGING IN THE 40S TO MID 50S ACROSS MUCH OF CENTRAL/SRN MO. WITH TIME...STRENGTHENING LOW/MID TROPOSPHERIC FLOW WILL RESULT IN MODEST NWD ADVECTION OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WITH LOWER/MID 50S DEW POINTS AS FAR NORTH AS SRN/CENTRAL MO BY LATE AFTN/EARLY EVENING AS TEMPERATURES WARM INTO THE LOWER 70S. STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES EVIDENT ON 12Z OUN/DDC/AMA SOUNDINGS WILL ADVECT EWD INTO MO/NRN AR THIS AFTN/EVENING. DESPITE SOMEWHAT LIMITED LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE...STEEP LAPSE RATES AND STRENGTHENING WIND FIELDS WILL RESULT IN A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR SEVERE TSTM DEVELOPMENT IN THE 20-22Z TIME FRAME IN THE ENHANCED AND WRN PORTIONS OF THE SLIGHT RISK AREA. STRONG FORCING FOR ASCENT AND DIURNAL HEATING WILL REMOVE CONVECTIVE INHIBITION FROM NEAR THE SFC LOW SWD ALONG THE DRYLINE INTO ERN OK/NWRN AR. WITH DEEP-LAYER SHEAR AVERAGING 50 KTS ORIENTED ORTHOGONAL TO THE DRYLINE...SUPERCELL STORMS WILL LIKELY BE THE DOMINANT MODE WITH LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS THE PRIMARY THREATS. THUNDERSTORMS SHOULD INITIATE ALONG THE WARM FRONT LATE THIS AFTERNOON WITH A SEVERE THREAT DEVELOPING ACROSS PARTS OF SW AND SCNTRL MO. mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT IS INCREASING WITH LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS POSSIBLE THROUGH THIS EVENING. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP BY 20-21Z IN FAR SE KS WITH COVERAGE INCREASING THEREAFTER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH A WELL-DEFINED AND COMPACT SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ATTENDANT SURFACE LOW/TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL ENCOURAGE CONVECTIVE INITIATION IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS. INITIAL STORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED NEAR AND JUST SOUTH OF THE SURFACE LOW CURRENTLY ANALYZED IN SE KS...WITH LATER CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ANTICIPATED ALONG A PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/TRAILING COLD FRONT. A WARM FRONT IS ADVANCING NORTH RAPIDLY OVER SW MO...AND ADDITIONAL STORMS WILL FORM NORTH OF THE SURFACE LOW/WARM FRONT AS THE STRONG FORCING WITH THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVERSPREADS THE AREA. ALTHOUGH CONDITIONAL INSTABILITY REMAINS SOMEWHAT MODEST /MLCAPE VALUES RANGE FROM 500 TO 1500 J PER KG IN THE NARROW WARM SECTOR ADVECTING NORTHEAST AHEAD OF THE FRONT/...INCREASING DEEP-LAYER SHEAR ASSOCIATED WITH A 50-60 KT MID-LEVEL SPEED MAX ORIENTED LARGELY ORTHOGONAL TO THE FRONT WILL SUPPORT INITIAL DISCRETE SUPERCELL MODES. A TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT INVOF THE WARM FRONT AND SURFACE LOW WHERE BOUNDARY LAYER WINDS WILL REMAIN BACKED IN THE INFLUENCE OF THE STRONG PRESSURE FALLS. OTHERWISE...SEVERE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY STORMS THAT DEVELOP...INCLUDING THOSE THAT SPREAD NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT IN 1000-1500 J/KG OF MUCAPE...UNTIL THE ABUNDANT CONVECTION IN THE WARM SECTOR DISRUPTS THE UNSTABLE PARCELS ASCENDING NORTH OF THE FRONT. DMGG WIND GUSTS ARE ALSO EXPECTED IN THE STEEP-LAPSE-RATE ENVIRONMENT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE TO EXPAND IN COVERAGE OVER THE AREA. SEVERE THREAT WILL CONTINUE THROUGH 00Z WITH THE MAIN THREAT BEING SEVERE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE TO EXPAND ALONG A FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS SW MO INTO FAR NW AR AND FAR NE OK. INITIAL CELLS HAVE BEEN DISCRETE BUT CLOSELY-SPACED. STORM INTERACTIONS HAVE PREVENTED LONG-LIVED SUPERCELL STRUCTURES THUS FAR...BUT ONE STORM HAS EMERGED AS DOMINANT AND HAS PRODUCED UP TO PING-PONG BALL SIZED HAIL FROM CRAWFORD COUNTY KANSAS TO BARTON COUNTY MISSOURI. A FEW ADDITIONAL CELLS ARE EXPECTED TO ORGANIZE FURTHER SOUTHWEST INTO FAR NW ARKANSAS...WHILE WIDESPREAD CONVECTION SPREADS NORTH OF THE SURFACE LOW WITH A CONTINUED SEVERE HAIL THREAT. A TORNADO OR TWO STILL CANNOT BE RULED WITH EFFECTIVE STORM-RELATIVE HELICITY VALUES 200-250 M2/S2 AND LOWER T/TD SPREADS INVOF THE WARM FRONT FOR ANY STORMS THAT CAN REMAIN DISCRETE. OTHERWISE THE MAIN THREAT WILL CONTINUE TO BE SEVERE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. FURTHER SOUTH INTO EASTERN OKLAHOMA CONVECTION HAS YET TO INITIATE ALONG THE FRONTAL ZONE AS CONVERGENCE AND FORCING FOR ASCENT WEAKENS CONSIDERABLY. LATEST HRRR GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT ANY STORMS THAT DO FORM ALONG THE FRONT IN THIS AREA WILL BE SHORT LIVED AND SUPPORT A MARGINAL HAIL THREAT FOR A FEW HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AREAS S AND SW OF WW 5 ARE BEING MONITORED FOR CONVECTIVE TRENDS THAT WOULD INDICATE SUBSTANTIAL BACKBUILDING OR NEW DEVELOPMENT. ANY SUSTAINED CONVECTION MAY PRODUCE STG/DAMAGING GUSTS AND SVR HAIL. ATTM AREA AFFECTED AND LIKELY TIME WINDOW FOR ANY SVR THREAT EACH APPEAR SMALL...RISK BEING MORE MRGL AND CONDITIONAL WITH SWWD EXTENT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWS LOW ESSENTIALLY COLLOCATED WITH SVR CONVECTION OVER SWRN MO IN WW 5...WITH COLD FRONT EXTENDING SWWD ACROSS ERN/SRN OK NEAR TQH...MKO...ADH...15 NNW ADM...THEN SWWD ACROSS NW TX JUST S SPS. FRONT SHOULD CONTINUE TO MOVE SEWD 10-15 KT...OVERTAKING DRYLINE THAT EXTENDS FROM FRONTAL INTERSECTION NEAR ADM...SSWWD BETWEEN RPH-MWL. CONFLUENCE LINE WAS EVIDENT ON SFC CHART BETWEEN ADM-MLC...CORRESPONDING WELL TO NNE-SSW-ORIENTED BUNCHING OF CONVECTIVE CLOUDS FROM HUGHES COUNTY OK SSWWD TOWARD DTO. FLOW HAS VEERED AHEAD OF DRYLINE AND W OF CONFLUENCE LINE...AND SHOULD REMAIN SO FOR AT LEAST A COUPLE MORE HOURS. FRONT AND CONFLUENCE LINE SHOULD REMAIN PRIMARY FOCI FOR TCU AND PSBL CB FOR A FEW MORE HOURS BEFORE ENOUGH DIABATIC COOLING OCCURS TO STRENGTHEN PRESENTLY WEAK MLCINH. NARROW CORRIDOR OF UPPER-50S TO LOW-60S F SFC DEW POINTS AND 11-12 G/KG MEAN MIXING RATIO...BENEATH 8 DEG C/KM MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...SUPPORTS MLCAPE 1500-2500 J/KG AS ESTIMATED FROM MODIFIED MODEL SOUNDINGS. TIME WINDOW OF OPTIMALLY WEAK CINH WILL BE THROUGH ABOUT 01Z. THOUGH 0-1-KM HODOGRAPHS ARE SMALL DUE TO VEERED/WEAK SFC WINDS...0-3 KM SRH AROUND 150 J/KG AND 35-45-KT EFFECTIVE-SHEAR MAGNITUDES MAY SUPPORT SOME TSTM ORGANIZATION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR POTENTIAL SHOULD DECLINE WITH EWD EXTENT AND WITH TIME...THOUGH ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND STG/DAMAGING GUSTS MAY OCCUR NEAR ERN FRINGES OF WW OR SLIGHTLY TO ITS E BEFORE ALL CONVECTION WEAKENS BELOW SVR LEVELS. REMAINDER WW CAN BE CLEARED W OF PRIMARY CONVECTIVE BAND. ANOTHER WW IS NOT LIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWED LOW AND COLD FRONT NOW BEHIND CONVECTION OVER SWRN MO...WHILE COLD FRONT EXTENDS SWWD ACROSS ERN OK. WARM FRONT EXTENDED FROM LOW ESEWD ACROSS SERN MO AND EXTREME WRN KY TO MID TN. BKN BAND OF TSTMS...INCLUDING OCNL/MRGL SUPERCELLS...ARE MOVING GENERALLY EWD 30-35 KT ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN MO AND OZARKS OF NWRN/N-CENTRAL AR. TSTMS ALREADY HAVE WEAKENED AND BECOME RATHER DISORGANIZED ACROSS CENTRAL MO N OF WARM FRONT. AS CONVECTION CONTINUES TO OUTRUN ALREADY NARROW CORRIDOR OF FAVORABLE SFC-BASED INSTABILITY...AND AS DIABATIC SFC COOLING INCREASES MLCINH...THIS TREND SHOULD CONTINUE THROUGH EVENING. AVBL RAOBS AND MODIFIED MODEL SOUNDINGS SUGGEST MLCAPE DECREASING FROM AROUND 1500 J/KG OVER SERN OK AHEAD OF CONVECTIVE BAND TO LESS THAN 250 J/KG IN VIH-UNO CORRIDOR...AND LIKELY TO DIMINISH WITH TIME. 50-60-KT EFFECTIVE-SHEAR MAGNITUDES AND 150-300 J/KG EFFECTIVE SRH -- WITH HIGHEST VALUES NEAR WARM FRONT -- ARE EXPECTED TO SUPPORT SOME STORM ORGANIZATION UNTIL BUOYANCY BECOMES TOO MEAGER. REF SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 136 FOR COVERAGE OF SVR THREAT S AND SW OF WW. ..EDWARDS.. 03/25/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
